content.body:
The Bf 109G was an improved model over the Bf 109F in some respects, and in some respects it wasn't always better. It boasted a high climb rate and top speed still, but in it's earlier versions without MW50 injection it was actually no faster than the F, and it's extra weight meant it didn't climb quite as well, although it still beat the Allied aircraft at climbing for the most part, except for the Spitfire IX.
The biggest surprise for those caught in its gunsights is going to be the "melon launcher" 30 mm Mk 108 cannon firing all HE mine rounds. This hits with roughly the same authority as a 40 mm Bofors round! However the increased weight does hurt its turn performance over that which could be extracted from the lighter more nimble 109F. The upside of this is that it's actually a little more stable to maneuver hard as a result of the loss of all that edgy nimbleness in it's leaner sister. Those who can't handle the feeling of instability in the 109F may find the heavier G more to their liking.
